M3.2-BOOT (CANONICAL STARTUP LAYER — MUST REMAIN AT THE BEGINNING OF THE FILE)
OMEGA-ISOP/M3.2
AUDIT ID: OI-STRUCT-ORGANIZATION-GLOBAL-AMALGAMATION-AUDIT-2026-10-28
DATE: 2026-10-28
STATUS: MATHEMATICAL AUDIT; NO CORE CHANGE; NO REGISTRATION CLAIM

TITLE
Organization from relations and compatibility: pairwise versus global amalgamation, and dynamical invariance

1. QUESTION

Do a relational structure and model-relative pairwise compatibility entail a global organization? If a global compatible structure exists, does that entail persistence under dynamics?

The answer to both entailment questions is no in general. Explicit additional conditions are required.

2. DEFINITIONS

Let C = {C1,...,Cn} be a finite family of constraints or component descriptions. Let CC(Ci,Cj)=1 mean that Ci and Cj admit a common admissible realization in the specified model. This is a model-relative pairwise predicate.

A global amalgamation of C is one realization satisfying all constraints C1,...,Cn simultaneously. Pairwise amalgamation and global amalgamation are different properties.

For a state space X and relational/constraint specification R, define the admissible set
Omega_R = {x in X : x satisfies every constraint in R}.

For a chosen evolution map T_t, invariance of Omega_R over a time interval I means
T_t(Omega_R) subseteq Omega_R for every t in I.
This is a dynamical condition, not merely a static compatibility condition.

3. COUNTERMODEL A: PAIRWISE COMPATIBILITY DOES NOT ENTAIL GLOBAL AMALGAMATION

Take Boolean variables x,y,z in {0,1}, and constraints:
C1: x != y
C2: y != z
C3: z != x

Each pair of constraints is jointly satisfiable:
- C1 and C2: choose (x,y,z) = (0,1,0).
- C2 and C3: choose (x,y,z) = (0,0,1).
- C1 and C3: choose (x,y,z) = (0,1,1).

Thus every pair has a common realization.

But all three constraints cannot be satisfied simultaneously with only two Boolean values. If x != y and y != z, then x = z, contradicting z != x. Therefore no global amalgamation exists.

Conclusion A:
Pairwise CC(Ci,Cj)=1 for every pair does not entail a global amalgamation of the whole family. A pairwise compatibility graph alone cannot establish global organization.

Scope note: this is a generic constraint-satisfaction countermodel establishing the logical point. It is not a claim that the Frozen Core itself specifies these Boolean constraints.

4. COUNTERMODEL B: STATIC ORGANIZATION DOES NOT ENTAIL DYNAMICAL PERSISTENCE

Let X = {a,b}, and let the constraint-defined admissible set be Omega_R = {a}. A global admissible structure therefore exists at the initial time.

Define an evolution map T by T(a)=b and T(b)=b. Then
T(Omega_R) = {b},
and {b} is not a subset of Omega_R.

The organization exists statically but is not invariant under this evolution.

By contrast, if a chosen T satisfies T(Omega_R) subseteq Omega_R, then Omega_R is invariant under that map. This conclusion is conditional on the invariance premise; it is not derived from the mere existence of Omega_R.

Conclusion B:
Static compatibility or global amalgamation does not entail persistence. Persistence requires a relation between the admissible set and the specified dynamics.

5. MINIMAL CONDITIONAL RESULT

If:
(i) the family of constraints is explicitly defined;
(ii) a single global realization satisfying all constraints exists; and
(iii) the chosen dynamics preserves the admissible set, T_t(Omega_R) subseteq Omega_R throughout the interval I;

then the organization represented by Omega_R persists as an admissible organization throughout I.

This is a conditional theorem from the stated premises. It does not establish that such a global realization or such dynamics must exist.

For robustness under perturbations, an additional perturbation class and a quantitative stability criterion must be specified. Invariance under one exact evolution does not automatically imply robustness.

6. WHAT IS REQUIRED TO MAKE ORGANIZATION A TESTABLE LEVEL

A concrete organization claim needs at least:
A. A specified family of components or constraint descriptions.
B. A precise model-relative meaning of pairwise compatibility.
C. A global amalgamation rule or a theorem guaranteeing global consistency; pairwise checks alone are insufficient in general.
D. A specified state space and a realization of the constraints.
E. A specified evolution law and an invariance or persistence condition.
F. If physical: operational observables, a measurement protocol, quantitative predictions, uncertainty/tolerance rules, and a failure condition.

These items are a research interface, not a claim that all of them are already derived from the Frozen Core.

7. DERIVATION LEDGER

Derived here:
- Pairwise satisfiability does not generally imply joint satisfiability; Countermodel A proves this.
- Existence of an admissible set does not generally imply invariance under a chosen evolution; Countermodel B proves this.
- Global existence plus an explicitly assumed invariance condition yields conditional persistence of the admissible organization.

Not derived here:
- A universal global-amalgamation principle.
- A unique organization from R or CC alone.
- A unique evolution law.
- Persistence from static compatibility alone.
- A physical organization law or new empirical prediction from Primitive Difference alone.

8. RELATION TO THE FROZEN CORE

The audit preserves the existing model-relative interpretation of CC: CC(C1,C2)=1 iff an admissible amalgamation exists for the specified pair in the specified model. It does not reinterpret CC as universal causation and does not infer global amalgamation from pairwise CC.

No Frozen Core text is changed or proposed as silently amended. This audit does not establish CE-V promotion, canonical acceptance, or RL registration. No registration status is asserted.

9. RESULT

Organization is not yet entailed merely by the presence of relations, pairwise compatibility, or persistence of individual distinctions. A defensible organization-level result requires a global compatibility condition and, for persistence, an explicit dynamical invariance condition. Physical status additionally requires operational realization and falsifiable quantitative consequences.
